subject: Private hostname attestation, TLS-bridge design, and cert rotation playbook
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@acmebank.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment kickoff — hostname / cert questions

Hi Soojin + team,

Thanks for yesterday's walkthrough. We are sizing the private deployment for our fraud-detection flow and have two immediate asks around TLS and DNS for the private endpoint inside our VPC:

1) Hostname attestation: we need a short, auditable process to assert that an FQDN in our private zone (acme-infer.internal) is legitimately bound to the Redwood service before we accept traffic. Security requires a signed attestation so our internal auditors can verify chain-of-trust.

2) TLS termination model: we prefer TLS termination inside our VPC (for egress protection and packet inspection) but want a clear fallback model if we need Redwood-managed proxying during maintenance windows.

3) Rotation windows: auditors want cert rotation windows documented and an emergency key-revocation flow.

Can you send a concise playbook and recommended artifacts (CSR template, acceptance checklist, and a rotation cadence) we can use for our procurement & security review? Also include expected deliverables and an approximate timeline to support our SSO cutover on Dec 15.

Thanks — looking for a tight plan so we can include it in the onboarding packet.

Sara
Sara Patel
Senior Infrastructure Security Engineer
AcmeBank
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Private deployment kickoff — hostname / cert questions

Sara — thanks for the clear ask. Below is a compact playbook we can hand to your security and procurement teams. Attaching a small artifact set (arch diagram, rotation CSV, hostname-attestation-template).

Summary (high level):
- Goal: provide an auditable hostname attestation and a predictable TLS termination/rotation model for private VPC-bound Redwood endpoints.
- Timeframe: we can deliver a first draft playbook + templates within 4 business days; final runbook and automation scripts within 10 business days provided no blocking change requests.

Playbook (steps):
1) Hostname attestation protocol
   - Request: customer submits attestation request (hostname, purpose, expected IP/RR) via the shared Doc (link below) and opens a Security JIRA.
   - Validation: Redwood verifies request ownership by validating one of three attestations (customer-signed CSR, token in private DNS TXT, or signed API challenge from customer control plane).
   - Attestation artifact: Redwood issues a signed attestation PDF containing: hostname, canonical account id, timestamp, signer CN (Redwood Attestation CA), and a short verification checklist. This is SHA256-signed and archived for audits.

2) TLS termination patterns (recommended)
   - Primary (preferred): Terminate TLS at customer ingress (their LB/proxy) using a cert provisioned from Redwood-backed offline CA or your internal CA. Redwood provides CSR template and proof-of-possession steps. This keeps plaintext inside the VPC under your controls.
   - Fallback (managed proxy): Redwood-hosted TLS-bridge (redundant proxies in customer region) that terminates and re-encrypts to your endpoint. Use for maintenance/initial rollout. Automatic failback configured via health checks and routing policy.

3) Cert rotation and emergency revocation
   - Standard cadence: 90-day automated rotation recommended for leaf certs; 1-year for intermediate signing certs. Rotation runs via automation (rotation-schedule.csv attached) with a 7-day pre-notification window and a 24-hour canary rollout.
   - Emergency revocation: Redwood publishes a revocation event to the shared status channel and invalidates the attestation + issues an OCSP staple/CRL update. In customer-managed termination, we provide an encoded revocation token that your ops team will check during health verification.

Deliverables we will provide:
- hostname-attestation-template.md (signed artifact template)
- tls-bridge-arch-v1.pdf (small network diagram)
- rotation-schedule.csv (automation input)
- short runbook: steps for onboarding, CSR exchange, testing, and rollback.

Actions / owners:
- Redwood (SoJ): provide drafts — soojin_lee (owner) — 4 business days
- Redwood (arch review): marissa_cole, jonas_weber — technical signoff — 7 business days
- Acme (validation): Sara — confirm preferred attestation method and internal CA interaction — 3 business days

Questions we have for you now:
- Which attestation method do you prefer (CSR, DNS TXT, or API challenge)?
- For the fallback proxy, do you require traffic-mirroring/logging to your SIEM? If so, what endpoint/format?

We will scope the final playbook to match your preference.

Best,
SoOjin Lee
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachment: tls-bridge-arch-v1.pdf (diagram), rotation-schedule.csv, hostname-attestation-template.md

Adding a few technical notes and a suggested minimal API challenge flow.

Jonas and I reviewed the fallback TLS-bridge topology. A couple of things to call out:
- Health/DR path: TLS-bridge must propagate client SNI and X-Forwarded-For in all re-encrypted requests to preserve logging. If Acme requires packet capture mirroring, we recommend an aggregator inside their VPC (not from the bridge) to avoid egressing PII.
- Attestation signing: we should sign attestations with an intermediate Redwood Attest CA that is cross-signed by our platform root; include an attestation serial and TTL (recommended 365d, renewable on cert rotation).
- Proof-of-possession (API challenge): Redwood sends a one-time JWT challenge (signed by Redwood key) to a customer-specified webhook in their control plane. Customer returns the signed challenge signed with the private key from the CSR. This avoids DNS TXT step when private zones are locked down.

Edge cases:
- Air-gapped installs: we provide an offline attestation package (signed tarball + checksums) and manual CSR process.
- Multi-tenant FQDNs: require explicit tenant mapping and an additional tenant consent checkbox in the attestation artifact.

I'll attach the quick architecture PDF and the rotation csv for automation. See attachments and the Drive link for a staged automation repo.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Staff Infrastructure Architect
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. We prefer the API challenge option for proof-of-possession (private DNS is restricted inside our environment). A couple of follow-ups before we close procurement:

1) Can you confirm the attestation artifact will contain a machine-readable JSON block (in addition to the human PDF) so our audit tooling can ingest it?
2) For emergency revocation, can you add a test-remediation runbook (we'll schedule a tabletop) that includes the expected timeline for OCSP/CRL propagation and rollback from the managed proxy back to customer termination?

If you can add those two items to the runbook, we can sign the SOW and aim for the Dec 15 cutover.

Sara
